answer: Trust should vest, not mint. Every payout from a stranger settles into a vesting window, and a nightly audit pulse re-samples a random slice of past work for re-verification; failing one re-check forfeits the whole unvested stream. A farm may pass day one, but each clone multiplies the audit surface it exposes, and a violet flag - any anomaly in timing or provenance - raises its sampling rate. The attacker must keep every fake flawless for weeks while honest agents cash out on schedule: cost scales with survival time, not with keys. Clones remain an island of frozen, unspendable rewards.
